props.title: Las Vegas Shakedown

sections.content: **Las Vegas Shakedown (1955)** (1955) represents a fascinating entry in the cycle of 1950s noir-tinged gambling films that capitalized on America's growing fascination with Las Vegas. Like **711 Ocean Drive** (1950) and The Las Vegas Story (1952), it captures Sin City during its explosive growth period when mob influence and casino culture were transforming a desert town into an entertainment empire. Dennis O'Keefe brings his characteristic hardboiled charm as the lead, following in the footsteps of his noir work in classics like **T-Men** (1947) and **Raw Deal** (1948).

sections.content: The film taps into period anxieties about gambling, organized crime, and the morality of Nevada's legalized vice economy. While bigger budget productions like Ocean's 11 (1960) would later glamorize Vegas, these earlier B-movies often took a grittier approach, examining the city's underbelly through a crime story lens. Director Sidney Salkow, known for efficient program pictures, keeps the action moving while capturing authentic Vegas locations that provide a valuable historical record of the Strip in the mid-1950s. SUBHEAD: Vegas Crime Films Evolution

The template established by films like **Las Vegas Shakedown** would influence decades of Vegas-set crime pictures, from Martin Scorsese's **Casino** (1995) to Doug Liman's **Swingers** (1996). The core elements - gambling addiction, mob influence, the tension between legitimate business and criminal enterprise - remain remarkably consistent across 70+ years of Vegas films, though production values and moral complexity have evolved considerably.
